AN ORDINANCE OF THE TOWN OF RESACA, GEORGIA FOR THE PURPOSE OF REGULATION OF NUISANCES; REGULATION OF NUISANCE CAUSED BY OPERATION OF OFF-ROAD MOTORIZED VEHICLES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES, AT THE REGULAR MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF RESACA HELD APRIL 8, 2014.______________________________________________________________________________

WHEREAS, the Town Council of the Town of Resaca, Georgia, finds that the operation of certain off-road motor vehicles, typically referred to as “four wheelers,” ATVs, or off road vehicles, disturbs the quiet enjoyment of residential tranquility within the city limits of Resaca; and

WHEREAS, the Town Council finds that it would be in the best interest of public health, safety and general welfare to regulate the operation of off-road motor vehicles; and

WHEREAS, it is within the police power of the Town of Resaca to adopt reasonable ordinances to promote the public health, safety and welfare;

NOW THEREFORE THE COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF RESACA, GEORGIA ORDAINS, and it is hereby ordained, pursuant to its Home Rule authority under the Georgia Constitution and the powers granted the Town in its Charter, that the following ordinance is adopted:
3: This Ordinance shall be known as the Town of Resaca Nuisance Ordinance.
4: This ordinance is intended to regulation the operation of off-road motorized vehicles that have the potential to, when operated in the evening, disturb the quiet enjoyment of residential tranquility within the city limits of Resaca and thereby constitute a nuisance.
5: “Off-road motorized vehicle” means any motorized vehicle designed for off-road use, commonly referred to as all-terrain vehicles, also known as “ATVs,” “Side-by-Sides,” “Four-wheelers,” “gators,” “mules,” etc.
6: A. It shall be unlawful to operate any off-road motorized vehicle after sunset or before sunrise if the operation of such vehicle is audible on any adjacent property containing a residence or residences.
7:
A. It shall not be a violation to operate off-road motorized vehicles as set forth in Section 4 in the event of an emergency, including but not limited to, severe weather events.

B. The restrictions of Sec. 4 shall not apply to government-owned vehicles being operated in the course of official duties.
8: Any violation of this Ordinance shall be a misdemeanor, and shall be punishable by citation to the municipal court. Any person convicted shall be subject to a minimum fine of $100 for the first offense, and a minimum fine of $250 for the second offense. The maximum fine shall be $500. Other lawful sentences may be imposed by the municipal court, including imprisonment up to 60 days, probation or community service,.
9: Any existing ordinances inconsistent with the provisions of this Ordinance are hereby repealed.
10: This Ordinance shall be effective April 9, 2014, the public health, safety and welfare demanding. This Ordinance was adopted the 8th day of April, 2014.
